text:
Trevor Moore has been a Kings fixture for years, and this is one of his tougher starts. He has five points in 15 games at more than 16 minutes a night, and Los Angeles has only 42% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, ten points worse than without him.

His own finishing is normal (two goals on 2.1 expected), so this isn't bad luck. It's a line that's getting outplayed while the rest of the Kings mostly aren't. That matters on a team that's outchancing opponents and still losing.

He grew up in Thousand Oaks, undrafted, and turned himself into a 448-game King after starting in Toronto. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says his offense lives in transition: 59% of his shots came off the rush last season. Evolving-Hockey had him a solid middle-six forward in 2025-26. Our projection sees about 18 goals. We'd watch for a line change before we'd watch his point total.
